title: Choosing Your Wife Everyday
author: Foundation Father
summary: A men's/marriage newsletter argues that the wedding-day vow is only the opening move of a marriage, not its substance — the real commitment is the daily, ongoing choice to remain faithful and present, which a loveless marriage, a wandering eye, or an affair each independently negate regardless of what was said at the altar. Its central psychological argument is about an asymmetry that develops over time: as a man grows older, more accomplished, and more responsible, his attractiveness and options tend to increase, while his wife's market prospects, by the piece's account, tend to diminish — and she rationally knows this, having chosen him on faith and potential rather than on the finished man he would become. The piece argues this asymmetry makes a wife's insecurity about her husband's ongoing choice of her rational rather than needy, dismisses the commonly cited "women file for 70% of divorces" statistic as not settling the underlying responsibility question, and reframes what a wife actually wants: not a husband with no options, but one who has real options and continues to choose her anyway — coming home daily, keeping his word, and maintaining his stated boundaries even under pressure.
points: The piece's core reframe is that marriage is not a single choice made at the altar but a choice that must be actively remade every day — a loveless marriage or a wandering eye negates the wedding vow regardless of what was said on that day.

It argues a structural asymmetry emerges over a marriage: a husband's attractiveness and options tend to rise as he grows more accomplished and responsible, while a wife's prospects, in the piece's account, tend to diminish — making her awareness of this shift rational rather than insecure.

It reframes the commonly cited "women file for 70% of divorces" statistic as incomplete, arguing it doesn't settle who bears responsibility for a marriage's health and doesn't account for the remaining 30%.

The piece's definition of what a wife actually wants is specific: not a husband with no other options, but one who has real options and continues to choose her anyway, validating the faith she placed in his potential when she married him.

It closes on an explicit call to consistency under pressure — keeping your word and "maintaining your frame" even when you've told her no, especially when you've told her no — as the practical content of daily fidelity.
quotes: Marriage is not choosing your wife. It's choosing your wife every day. By marrying your wife, you made an active choice. But you must keep making that same active choice every day for the rest of your life.
Yet your wife chose you before you gained all of this attractiveness. She chose you based on your potential. She chose you based on faith.
So, if you are not actively choosing her every day, she is rational in feeling a bit insecure. Men leave the wives of their youth for younger models all of the time. It's a cliché.

Your wife wants you to get more attractive. That's what she expected when she married you all those years ago. She wants other women to see how attractive you are. She wants to brag about the husband she chose.

What your wife wants is for you to have lots of other options…and then choose her, no matter what. To choose her every day. To come home every day. To love her and cherish her, words still included in many vows.
She chose you when you were still a boy. Choose her after you have become a man.
